On this Mac · nothing sent anywhere

Frank, 58, runs a small plumbing supply. Two staff, thin margins, a shoebox of receipts, and three hard years. One day with an AI team that does the paperwork and asks before anything leaves.

Frank is invented. This is the product we're building.

6:45 AM

The shop opens without him.

Frank has run the plumbing supply for eleven years, with two staff and margins that have gone. This morning the opening routine is on the screen behind the counter: what needs doing, who's doing it, ticked as it's done. Frank sees it from the kitchen.

7:10 AM

The books, from a photo.

Every receipt and invoice gets photographed by whoever has it. By morning it's read, categorised and marked "unchecked". Frank looks, fixes one, and that fix becomes the rule.

7:20 AM

Not an accountant. Gets you to one.

At the end of the month the ledger exports in a form his accountant takes, with every line traceable to its photo. True Convo doesn't do his tax. It makes the tax hour cost an hour.

11:00 AM

A team that does the paperwork.

A trade customer wants a quote for a 40-radiator job. A quoting specialist drafts it from the stock list and the supplier prices; a stock checker says what's short; each reports in its own words. Frank reads both, changes a margin, and sends it himself.

11:20 AM

Not instead of his people.

Dev and Lena are on the counter and in the van. The specialists do the quotes, the chasing, the listings and the books, so the two humans can do the work customers come in for.

11:40 AM

Every hand-off, visible.

Frank sees who was asked what, what came back, and what it cost. Nothing is sent, ordered or paid without his yes, every time.

3:00 PM

Hiring someone who'll care.

3:30 PM

Wait, what?

An applicant's reference mentions a "settlement agreement". Frank highlights it, right-clicks, and an outsider explains it plainly, on the shop's own Mac, without reading anything else.

4:00 PM

The numbers, at the kitchen table.

Cash in, cash out, what's due, what's owed, and which three things would change the month. In plain words, from his own ledger, on a model running on his Mac.

7:20 PM

Build the thing the shop needs.

Frank wants a board for the van: today's drops, what's on it, signed-for or not. He describes it. A builder makes it, a checker tries to break it, and it runs on the shop's Mac and Lena's phone.

7:40 PM

No frontier model required.

Everything today ran on the shop's own Mac. Nothing went to the cloud, because nothing needed to. If a bigger brain is ever worth paying for, it's his key and his yes, each time.

What the shop keeps.

Its people. The specialists do paperwork. Dev and Lena do the work customers come in for. Nobody is replaced by a chat window.
Its books. Every line traceable to a photo, on the shop's own Mac, exported to the accountant Frank already has.
Its decisions. Nothing is sent, ordered, paid, posted or hired without Frank's own yes.
Its privacy. Customers' names, prices and margins never leave the shop unless Frank sends them.
Open core. Copy it, change it, label it as the shop's own.
Leave any time. Export everything in a form that works without us.

Not on your own

More than software.

True Convo is meant to come with people: lessons in plain words, others in the same spot as Frank, and the apps and templates they make and share.

ComingLearn

Bookkeeping for a small shop, ten minutes at a time, in words that aren't an accountant's.

ComingPeople

Other owners down the road and across the country, trading what kept them open.

ComingShared

A staff rota app and a supplier-order sheet another owner made. Some free, some a few pounds to the maker.

None of this exists yet. It's what we hope to build with the first people who use True Convo, and we'll say so plainly until it's real.

11:00 PM

The shop closed. The books were done.

A quote sent, a job posted, three people shortlisted, the month understood, and a van board built, all on the shop's own Mac. Nothing left it today. No account with us. No ads. Nothing sold on.

Where this stands. True Convo is in development and not out yet. Built so far: the pill, dictation at the cursor, the Desk with a model on the Mac, encrypted storage, and the first engines for lists, habits, tasks, the agenda, mail, the calendar, time, sources and the capture inbox. Being built now: the PA, the iPhone, sync and the first-run guide. Specialists working together, the books, hiring, the checkup and building his own apps come after launch; the phone assistant is a paid module, later. The lessons, the community and the shared library are a plan too; none of them exist yet. Frank and everything on this page are invented to show the plan; the tests decide the order.
